main_theorem_refuted_scope: Only the literal covariance component Theorem 1.2(v) is refuted as written. Harnack, uniform capacity, Sobolev existence, and conditional attainment results are not refuted by this report.

issues.label: Energy of the admissible density in the Harnack step

For any fixed integer L>=2 set delta_H=1/(8L), R=8Ln,n>=2,delta=1/2,epsilon=1; h(j)=2R+clamp(j,-R,R) is positive and harmonic throughout B(0,R).

issues.decisive_evidence: With m=(16L-1)n+2,M=(16L+1)n,q=2n-2, exact modulus is 1/(q+1). For a_j=log((m+j+1)/(m+j))/log(M/m), v has values a0,a0,a1,...,a(q-1) on the crossing interval and zero outside. E(v)=a0^2+a(q-1)^2+sum(aj-a(j-1))^2<=3(M/(mq))^2. issues.label: False direction of the advertised energy-measure covariance
issues.status: supported literal main-property counterexample; inverse correction derived; author adoption unverified
issues.source_location: Selected source p6 Theorem1.2(v), p61 Proposition8.15(e) and its proof, pushforward convention p60(8.16), D4 p49; cutoff pp38–39, weak locality pp61–62. Long v4 pp8,112–113.
issues.hypotheses: Any p>1 on the actual carpet. Let a=(-1,-1), Phi the quarter-turn pi/2, r=1/16, C=closedB(a,2r). The valid continuous Fp cutoff f=psi_{a,r} is1 on B(a,r), zero outside C, and nonconstant in Lp(m) by full support. Scalar symmetry gives f composed Phi in Fp; locality applies to open zero regions.
issues.suspect_step: Phi_*Gamma[f]=Gamma[f composed Phi] is stated for all D4, but standard pushforward requires the inverse composition. In the proof, cylinders correspond to Phi(A), while the final line uses Phi^-1(A).
issues.decisive_evidence: nu=Gamma[f] has nu(K)=E_p(f)>0 and support in C. g=f composed Phi vanishes outside Phi^-1 C. Centers Phi a and Phi^-1 a are distance1, each set radius1/8, so an open neighborhood of Phi C has g=0 and Gamma[g](Phi C)=0. Yet (Phi_*nu)(Phi C)=nu(C)=E_p(f)>0. Does not assume ordinary coordinate functions belong to Fp or use the disputed identity.
issues.method: Analytic counterexample using the paper's proved cutoff, positivity and locality; direct cylinder-set derivation of the correction; actual theorem/convention/proof views.
issues.counterevidence_and_alternatives: The formula is valid for involutions such as reflections and the half-turn, but D4 includes quarter-turns. Standard inverse-image pushforward is explicit in(8.16). Scalar energy invariance does not reverse set transport. Selected source and acquired later long version retain the same missing inverse. Journal-final and unacquired revisions not claimed checked.
issues.repair: Gamma[f composed Phi]=(Phi^-1)_*Gamma[f], equivalently Phi_*Gamma[f]=Gamma[f composed Phi^-1]. Closed-set cylinder limits give Gamma[f composed Phi](A)=Gamma[f](Phi(A)); regularity extends to all Borel sets.
issues.dependency: Theorem1.2(v) is an advertised core property of the energy-measure family. Existence, total mass, self-similarity and scalar invariance are separate results, not refuted.
issues.severity_basis: Literal main covariance guarantee gives distinct masses on a concrete Borel set; a short inverse correction does not erase this false statement. No broader downstream collapse asserted.

issues.label: Vertex modulus short-path bound omits the endpoint vertex
issues.source_location: Selected source pp14–16, Lemma2.4 equation(2.2), uses checked pp19–21.
issues.hypotheses: The finite connected simple two-vertex one-edge graph, path family containing that path, p=2,L=1. Defined path length counts edges, density length sums over the path's vertex set.
issues.suspect_step: Existence of a path of edge length<=L is claimed to imply Mod>=L^{1-p}.
issues.decisive_evidence: For the one-edge path, min(rho(a)^2+rho(b)^2) with rho(a)+rho(b)>=1 is1/2, attained at1/2,1/2; the printed bound is1. Exact rational diagnostics retained for L=1,2,3,10.
issues.method: Exact finite counterexample, general Holder proof and equality case.
issues.counterevidence_and_alternatives: Reading L as vertex count would repair the statement but contradicts the defined edge length. Actual source views remove extraction ambiguity.
issues.repair: If s distinct vertices lie on the given path, s<=L+1. Holder gives sum rho^p>=s^{1-p}>=(L+1)^{1-p}; direct sum for p=1. Simple paths with uniform density attain equality.
issues.dependency: Checked applications pp19–21 need only a fixed multiplicative estimate; (L+1)^{1-p}>=2^{1-p}L^{1-p} for L>=1.
issues.severity_basis: Local numerical normalization; no change to an exponent or essential conclusion established, so Minor rather than an additional Major.
